rounds.text: Jeevan Scientific Technology Ltd is experiencing a powerful fundamental acceleration, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 87% [E17] and a staggering 263% jump in compounded profit growth over the same period [E21]. This explosive performance is translating into material margin expansion, with operating margins surging to 22% in the TTM period—an impressive 11 percentage point increase over three years [E30]—and reaching 25% in the September 2026 quarter [E31]. Furthermore, the company benefits from a robust sector backdrop with healthcare operating under a clear positive tailwind score of +0.76 [E64]. Market multiples look attractive relative to peers, with an EV/EBITDA of 9.95x comparing favourably to a sector benchmark of 16.64x [E11], and both a P/E of 22x and P/B of 2.29x trading at discounts to their respective sector benchmarks [E6, E7]. Finally, balance sheet liquidity remains comfortable, supported by a current ratio of 2.38x as of March 2025 [E38] and moderate leverage at 0.35x [E37]. Conceded: [E13], [E36], [E43], [E51].

The current market price of ₹90.3 carries a heavy valuation disconnect, as a discounted cash flow model explicitly places the intrinsic value at ₹44 per share, resulting in a severe negative margin of safety of -103.4% [E43, E44]. Furthermore, reported earnings fail to translate into actual cash generation, highlighted by a poor cash conversion ratio of 0.41x and a deep free cash flow deficit of -7.76 Cr as of March 2026 [E34, E36]. Fundamental profitability metrics remain chronically depressed, evidenced by a multi-year median return on equity of 0% over the last 3 years and a depressed 3-year low ROE flagged at -0.01% [E28, E52]. Compounding these operational and valuation risks, promoter commitment is actively retreating, with holdings dropping by 8.48 percentage points over three years down to 30.00% [E41, E53], alongside an absence of dividend returns for shareholders [E4, E50]. Borrowings have simultaneously climbed to ₹26.76 Cr by September 2026 from ₹21.28 Cr a year prior, increasing the financial burden on the company [E39]. Conceded: the company displays strong trailing twelve-month sales growth of 87% and a significant 263% surge in trailing profit growth [E17, E21].

Conceded: the discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at ₹44 with a negative margin of safety [E43, E44], and free cash flow stands at -7.76 Cr [E36]. However, relying solely on static DCF models ignores an operational inflection where TTM sales grew 87% and profit surged 263% [E17, E21], outperforming expectations as profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 216% [E47]. The historical median ROE metrics cited by the bear reflect past headwinds and miss the dramatic operational turnaround [E28, E52, E63], evidenced by operating margins expanding to 22% in TTM against 12% three years earlier (+11 percentage points) and reaching 25% in the September 2026 quarter [E30, E31]. Conceded: borrowings increased to ₹26.76 Cr [E39], but this is backed by comfortable short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 2.38x [E38] and ongoing capital deployment into capital work-in-progress standing at ₹5.66 Cr [E40]. Finally, while promoter holding decreased [E41], the business trades at an attractive EV/EBITDA of 9.95x against a sector benchmark of 16.64x [E11] while operating within a strongly supportive healthcare sector tailwind [E62].

Conceded: TTM sales grew 87% and profit surged 263% [E17, E21], and operating margins expanded to 22% in the TTM and 25% in the September 2026 quarter [E30, E31]. However, this surging profit is entirely divorced from actual cash generation, evidenced by a dismal cash conversion of 0.41x and a severe free cash flow burn of -7.76 Cr [E34, E36]. Conceded: the current ratio sits at a comfortable 2.38x [E38] and the company is investing in capital work-in-progress of 5.66 Cr [E40], but borrowings have simultaneously climbed to 26.76 Cr [E39] while promoters continue to dump their stake down to 30.00% [E41]. Furthermore, dismissing historical ROE as stale [E28, E52, E63] ignores the reality of a 10-year median ROE of 3% and a 3-year median of 0% [E26, E28], which proves that structural capital destruction is far more frequent than these temporary margin spikes. Finally, while the EV/EBITDA of 9.95x appears discounted against sector benchmarks [E11], the market price of 90.3 sits a staggering 103.4% above the DCF intrinsic value of 44 [E43, E44], making the valuation completely unsustainable regardless of sector tailwinds [E62].
